name: LMC6082AIMX_NOPB
title: Precision CMOS single, dual and quad op amps (LMC6081, LMC6082, LMC6084)
summary: CMOS operational amplifiers in single (LMC6081), dual (LMC6082) and quad (LMC6084) versions for 4.5 V to 15.5 V single supplies or ±2.25 V to ±7.75 V split supplies. Typical input bias current is 10 fA and offset 150 µV; the output swings to within 20 mV of the supply rail into 2 kΩ, and the input range includes the negative rail. Gain bandwidth is 1.3 MHz and supply current about 0.45 mA per amplifier. Two grades: AI (350 µV maximum offset) and I (800 µV).

circuits.title: Feedback capacitor cancelling input capacitance
circuits.description: An inverting stage with a large feedback resistor. CIN stands for the capacitance at the inverting input (source, photodiode or board strays). Cf across R2 is chosen so that R1·CIN ≤ R2·Cf, which restores phase margin and a clean pulse response.

parts.note: stray or source capacitance, not a fitted part

circuits.title: Non-inverting gain of 10 driving a capacitive load
circuits.description: Gain of 10 set by 90 kΩ and 10 kΩ, with the 90 kΩ taken from VOUT after a 20 Ω series resistor that feeds the 1000 pF load. A 20 pF capacitor from the amplifier output to the inverting input feeds the high-frequency part of the output back and preserves phase margin. V- grounded, 0.1 µF bypass on +V.

circuits.title: Follower with a pull-up resistor for a large capacitive load
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower driving capacitor C, with resistor R from the output to V+. A pull-up current of 500 µA or more improves the response into capacitive loads; R is sized from the amplifier's sink current and the output swing needed, and it changes the open-loop gain.

circuits.title: Three-amplifier instrumentation amplifier, gain about 100
circuits.description: Two non-inverting input buffers share a gain network (R1, R2 and its 2 kΩ trim, R5) and drive a difference stage (R3, R4, R6, R7). With R1 = R5, R3 = R6 and R4 = R7 the gain is (R2 + 2R1)/R2 × R4/R3, about 100 with R2 trimmed to 9.822 kΩ. The 2 kΩ pot sets the gain without disturbing CMRR; the 20 kΩ pot in R7 trims CMRR so the resistors need not be precision matched. Input resistance is above 10^14 Ω, input current below 100 fA, offset drift below 2.5 µV/°C, gain accuracy 0.01% at AV = 1000.

parts.note: amplifier A: inverting-side buffer; amplifier B: non-inverting-side buffer
gain trim in series with R2, wiper tied to one end
CMRR trim, used as a variable resistor

notes: VOUT / VIN = (R2 + 2R1)/R2 × R4/R3 when R1 = R5, R3 = R6 and R4 = R7.

circuits.title: Low-leakage sample and hold
circuits.description: One switch of a CD4066, driven by S/H, connects the input to a 0.1 µF polypropylene or polystyrene hold capacitor; an amplifier wired as a follower buffers the capacitor.

circuits.title: 1 Hz square-wave oscillator
circuits.description: A 1 Hz square-wave oscillator on a single +5 V rail. R1 (to +5 V), R3 (to ground) and R2 (from the output) set the non-inverting input, all 470 kΩ; R4 (10 MΩ) from the output and C1 (0.068 µF) to ground form the timing network at the inverting input.

circuits.title: Instrumentation amplifier, gain 10, with two RES11A networks
circuits.description: Each input drives a non-inverting buffer. A RES11A90 network (9 kΩ over 1 kΩ, twice) sets a gain of 10: each buffer's output feeds back through 9 kΩ to its inverting input, and the two 1 kΩ halves join between the inverting inputs. A RES11A10 network (four 1 kΩ) around the third amplifier forms a unity-gain difference stage referred to REF. C2 and C3 sit across the 9 kΩ feedback resistors; C1 filters the difference stage's non-inverting node to ground; the trimmer C4 across the output feedback 1 kΩ adjusts AC common-mode rejection. Input impedance is very high and the output is single-ended.

operation.text: LMC6081 (single), LMC6082 (dual) and LMC6084 (quad) are CMOS precision op amps for single supplies of 4.5 V to 15.5 V. The A grade (LMC608xAI) has tighter offset, gain, swing and short-circuit limits than the I grade (LMC608xI). Both run from -40 °C to 85 °C. LMC6082AIMX/NOPB is the A-grade dual in the 8-pin SOIC on a 2500-piece reel. The LMC6062 is the lower-power dual relative.

The output stage swings rail to rail even into heavy loads, with low output impedance and high gain; its compensation keeps it stable across more operating conditions than older micropower amplifiers. The input common-mode range takes in V- and stops about 1.9 V below V+. Input bias current rises when the common-mode voltage is large.

High-value feedback resistors combined with even a few picofarads at the inverting input (transducer, photodiode, board) eat phase margin and spoil the pulse response. A capacitor Cf across the feedback resistor R2 cancels it when R1·CIN ≤ R2·Cf. Guarding the inputs cuts both leakage and stray input capacitance.

The rail-to-rail output stage has gain and holds the compensation capacitor, so its dominant pole moves with the resistive load. Adding a resistor across a capacitive load lets the amplifier drive more capacitance (Figures 5-22 and 5-23). A capacitive load on the output adds a pole with the output impedance and costs phase margin, giving ringing or oscillation. Remedies: a series output resistor with feedback taken after it plus a small capacitor from the amplifier output to the inverting input, or a resistor from the output up to V+ that draws 500 µA or more, sized against the sink current and the swing needed; the pull-up also changes the open-loop gain.

Like other CMOS parts the amplifier contains a parasitic SCR whose gate behaves like the I/O pins. A trigger current into an I/O pin can latch it, and a holding current keeps it latched. Resistance in series with any capacitance that could dump current into an I/O pin, and current limiting in the supply leads, both reduce the risk.

Very high input impedance plus a small supply current suit battery instruments: hand-held pH probes, medical analysers, magnetic-field, gas and silicon pressure sensors, photodiode and infrared preamplifiers, piezoelectric charge amplifiers, DAC buffers, precision rectifiers, integrators, voltage references and sample-hold stages. Low-drift resistors such as the RES11A keep an instrumentation amplifier's CMRR over temperature.

Any circuit working below about 1000 pA of leakage needs special board layout; board surface leakage grows with humidity, dust and contamination. Surround the inputs, and every component lead tied to them, with a copper ring on both sides of the board, driven at the input voltage so no current can flow across it. Example: 10^12 Ω between a pad and a 5 V trace leaks 5 pA, a hundredfold worse than the amplifier itself; a guard within 5 mV of the input leaks only 0.05 pA even through 10^11 Ω. In an inverting stage the guard goes to ground (the non-inverting input's potential); in a non-inverting stage and in a follower it goes to the inverting-input node, which sits at the input voltage.

For a few circuits, an alternative to a guard ring is to keep the input pin out of the board altogether: bend it up and solder the input components straight to it, using air as the insulator, while all other pins go into the board.
